title: Sinica Weekend Edition: Three Days Out and About in Beijing
summary_zh: 本期周末特别节目中，主播Kaiser Kuo携带便携录音设备走上北京街头，记录了十月底至十一月初三天的真实生活切面。透过在Café Zarah、Golden Weasel酒吧、香港大学北京中心及餐桌旁的即兴对谈，节目串联起智库学者、艺术家、媒体人与经济学家对当下中国的微观体感与宏观观察。受访者们探讨了北京外籍社群与文艺生态在疫情后的温和复苏、中欧围绕新能源汽车与光伏出口的产业博弈、中国经济的“K型”分化与房地产深度调整，以及主动刺破地产泡沫与转向硬科技之间的政策逻辑。同时，跨国科研合作面临的安全化阻碍与在美中国留学生的夹缝处境，也折射出地缘政治张力下的个体困境，立体呈现出一座在剧烈变迁与日常惯性间交织的当代北京。
key_takeaways_zh: 面对中国新能源汽车与光伏等制造业出口浪潮，欧洲不应止步于防御性抱怨，而需提出双方均可接受的具体谈判诉求以达成利益平衡。
当下中国经济呈现显著的“K型”分化特征：硬科技与人工智能从业者信心高涨，而受房地产深度回调拖累的传统制造业与居民消费则持续承压。
监管层早年借“三条红线”主动刺破房地产泡沫，在深层逻辑上与引导资源流向人工智能、先进半导体等硬科技领域的国家战略密切相关。
在“武器化相互依赖”的地缘政治氛围下，跨国科研交流正遭受信任赤字侵蚀，而在美中国留学生也日益陷入“父母离异式”的选边站队困境。
尽管经历了街道整治、疫情冲击及对西方节日的降温，北京的外籍常住群体与本土文艺圈仍在“第三空间”中展现出复苏迹象与社群韧性。

highlights.title_zh: 北京外籍社群与标签反思
highlights.summary_zh: Kaiser Kuo剖析了“Expat”一词在亚洲语境下隐含的种族偏见，并解释了自己为何反感这一标签却依然珍视北京的外籍朋友。他指出，长期定居北京的外籍人士大多怀有理解这座城市的真诚意愿，外籍社群的构成与特质本身也是观察城市魅力的重要窗口。
highlights.quote_en: The kind of foreign community that a city draws to it says something meaningful about that city.

highlights.title_zh: 中欧产业博弈需明确诉求
highlights.summary_zh: 柏林非洲政策研究所的Olumide Abimbola分享了在保定参访光伏建筑一体化（BIPV）工厂时的震撼体验。谈及中国新能源汽车与工业品出口浪潮对德国及欧洲制造业的冲击，他认为欧洲不能仅停留在抱怨“不想要什么”，而必须明确提出建设性诉求并与中方谈判妥协。
highlights.quote_en: It's okay not to want something, but what do you want? And do you think what you want can be acceptable to the other side?

highlights.title_zh: 第三空间与中国议题表达困境
highlights.summary_zh: Golden Weasel酒吧联合创始人Anthony Tao阐释了酒吧作为凝聚同道者“第三空间”的社区价值。他还借法国球星姆巴佩引发的舆论风波指出，当下讨论中国议题犹如“薛定谔的猫”，任何单一维度的公开表态都会瞬间招致不同立场的反弹，个体几乎无法在公共舆论场完整还原复杂语境。
highlights.quote_en: Any individual's ability to paint a complete picture is insufficient. We are unable to.

highlights.title_zh: 北京胡同变迁与社群韧性
highlights.summary_zh: 定居北京近十五年的Amy回顾了从2012年黄金时期至今的城市氛围变迁。她坦言，尽管经历了胡同“开墙打洞”整治、疫情封控等重重挑战，在京常住群体依然依靠彼此连接维系着独特的生活方式，而社区酒吧则成为凝聚众人的灯塔。
highlights.quote_en: Even COVID, even like the 'brickening', everything. And we've still found a way.

highlights.title_zh: 港大北上揽才与科研脱钩隐忧
highlights.summary_zh: 前FT中文网总编辑、现就职于香港大学的Wang Feng介绍了港大在北京举办人才论坛以提升在京知名度的初衷。Kaiser Kuo则在圆桌发言中回顾了尼克松访华后中美学术交流委员会的历史贡献，并警示在“武器化相互依赖”的当下，技术安全化与互信缺失正严重威胁跨国科研合作。
highlights.quote_en: Today, in this age of weaponized interdependence, there is so much mistrust and there is suspicion of any scientific collaboration.

highlights.title_zh: K型经济分化与佛山楼市降温
highlights.summary_zh: 资深中国经济观察家Andy Rothman对官方在居民收入与消费增速放缓面前的淡定态度表示困惑，并认同当前中国经济呈现“K型”分化的判断。他结合近期调研指出，上海科技从业者普遍乐观，而受商品房销售面积较峰值暴跌约80%重创的家具建材之都佛山，民营企业家虽处境艰难但仍在顽强坚守。
highlights.quote_en: I'm trying to figure out why the government is not as nervous as I am about the continuing slowdown in income growth and consumption.

highlights.title_zh: 房地产去泡沫化与硬科技转向
highlights.summary_zh: Kaiser Kuo复盘了与上海交通大学经济学家朱宁的晚餐交流，重点提及朱宁将六年前“三条红线”主动刺破房地产泡沫与中国全力押注人工智能、先进半导体等硬科技联系起来的独到理论。此外，周末酒吧被明确要求不得举办万圣节主题活动，也折射出近年北京对西方节日庆祝的限制。
highlights.quote_en: connecting the deliberate deflation of the real estate bubble, you know, beginning with the Three Red Lines policy back six years ago, with China's push into AI

highlights.title_zh: 重返北京见闻与留美学生处境
highlights.summary_zh: 阔别八年重返北京的青年问题研究者Eric Fish感叹于满街新能源汽车与数字生活的无缝衔接，同时也注意到大规模基建落幕、房价大幅回调以及年轻人中延续已久的经济迷茫感。谈及近年对留美中国学生的研究，他形容这一群体如同身处“父母离异”拉扯中的孩子，越来越难维持跨国生活而被迫选边站队。
highlights.quote_en: it's more and more felt like kids with divorcing parents being pulled from both directions.

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Welcome to the Sinica Podcast, a weekly discussion of current affairs in China. In this program, we look at books, ideas, new research, intellectual currents, and cultural trends that can help us better understand what's happening in China's politics, foreign relations, economics, and society.
transcript.zh: 欢迎收听 Sinica Podcast，这是一档聚焦中国时事的每周深度访谈节目。在这里，我们探讨书籍、思想、最新研究、思潮与文化趋势，帮助大家更全面地理解中国的政治、对外关系、宏观经济与社会变迁。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Join me each week for in-depth conversations that shed more light and bring less heat to how we think and talk about China. I'm Kaiser Kuo, coming to you this week from Beijing.
transcript.zh: 每周请随我一同展开理性、深入的对话，少一些火药味，多一些真知灼见，共同审视我们该如何理解和探讨中国。我是 Kaiser Kuo，本周在北京向大家播报。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Listeners, please support my work by becoming a paying subscriber at sinicapodcast.com. I get how all these Substack subscriptions can really start to add up, so I try to offer you guys a lot.
transcript.zh: 各位听众，欢迎访问 sinicapodcast.com 成为付费订阅会员，支持我的工作。我非常理解各大 Substack 订阅费用累积起来确实是一笔不小的开销，因此我也竭尽所能为大家提供丰富的回馈内容。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: You get the Sinica Chinese Phrase of the Week from Andrew Methven. You get podcasts and roundups from the terrific folks at Trivium, the indispensable China Global South Podcast. You get historian James Carter's This Week in China's History.
transcript.zh: 您将收到 Andrew Methven 主笔的“Sinica 每周中文词汇”；欣赏到 Trivium 优秀团队出品的播客与资讯综述；收听不可或缺的 China Global South Podcast；还能阅读历史学者 James Carter 撰写的“中国历史上的本周”。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: You get the You Can Learn Chinese Podcast, and now, in a new weekly feature, a Europe-China perspective from Rhodium Group's Rene Rueschmeyer. So please do subscribe so I can continue to bring you those conversations and all that other good stuff.
transcript.zh: 不仅如此，还有 You Can Learn Chinese Podcast，以及最新推出的每周特栏——由荣鼎咨询（Rhodium Group）的 Rene Rueschmeyer 带来的中欧视角。欢迎大家踊跃订阅，支持我持续为您带来这些深度访谈与优质内容。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I wanted to do something different this week. In the time since I've come back to Beijing, I get asked a lot about what my day-to-day life here is like. It's understandable.
transcript.zh: 这期节目我想换个花样。自打搬回北京以来，身边总有人问我在这里的日常生活究竟是什么样子。这完全可以理解。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So I thought I'd bring a mic and a portable recorder along with me for the weekend to give listeners a sense for what it's like for me living in Beijing again. Weekdays are different. I mean, I just read a lot for upcoming shows, I try to write something, I prep for upcoming talks, I, of course, I edit the podcast and publish the other great stuff on Sinica, and lots more just work stuff.
transcript.zh: 所以这个周末，我干脆随身揣着麦克风和便携录音机，带大家沉浸式感受一下我重返北京后的日常。工作日的情形截然不同——我得为接下来的节目录制大量阅读，试着动笔写写东西，筹备近期的讲座，当然还要剪辑播客、在 Sinica 上发布各类优质内容，处理各种繁杂的案头工作。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yes, I also meet for lunch with my daughter or with some friends, and I usually squeeze in a band rehearsal or two. Weekdays, I, I hold a kind of informal office hours, I guess you could call it, at one of my favorite cafes in town, Cafe Zarah.
transcript.zh: 当然，我也会抽空陪女儿或朋友吃个午饭，每周通常还会挤出一两次乐队排练。工作日里，我基本上都在城里我最喜欢的一家咖啡馆——Cafe Zarah，甚至可以说在那里设立了非正式的“对外接待时间”。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And it seems a number of young people have figured out that they can find me there most days, and that, well, I'm more than happy to hear about their work, offer what advice I can about their academic interests or their careers, or just, just chat with them about what's on their mind when it comes to China, trade issues or tech or politics or the state of the economy or the discourse or music or anything at all.
transcript.zh: 不少年轻人似乎摸清了规律，知道平时多半能在那儿撞见我。我也非常乐意倾听他们的研究与工作，就学术兴趣或职业规划提供些建议，或是随性聊聊他们对中国的看法——无论是贸易纠纷、科技前沿、政治局势、宏观经济现状，还是公共舆论话语、音乐，任何话题都可以天马行空地聊。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So this weekend was all about life outside the home, which isn't typical, though the home, as it happens, is currently filled with moving boxes. On the last Thursday of October, just before we did this little weekend, Fanfan and I finally found the apartment that we want to rent for the next couple of years before we ship all of our stuff over and decide whether we're going to actually buy in Beijing.
transcript.zh: 因此，这个周末的主题完全是“户外生活”。虽然这并不算常态，但眼下家里确实堆满了搬家纸箱。就在十月的最后一个星期四，正好是录制这个周末片段的前夕，凡凡和我终于定下了一套打算长租两年的公寓。我们计划先过渡一阵，再把所有家当海运过来，最终决定是否在北京安家置业。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: More on the new place later, but there was a lot of incentive to be out of the apartment for the whole weekend. Before I dive...
transcript.zh: 关于新居后文再细表，不过这个周末倒确实让人有充分的理由在外面待上一整天。在切入正题之前……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Let me address something that I know will raise hackles with some listeners. I know that what follows is a bit heavy on foreigners, on, on so-called expatriates. I've actually long had a problem with that particular word.
transcript.zh: 让我先回应一个我知道可能会让部分听众感到不快的问题。我知道接下来的内容里，“外国人”、也就是所谓“外籍人士（expat）”的比重有点高。其实我一直对这个词抱有微词。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: For some reason, it seems, in the Asian context at least, to have come to mean white people living abroad. I never hear Chinese people living in the U.S. described as expats, despite my efforts to popularize that over the last decade living in North Carolina where there are a lot of Chinese expats.
transcript.zh: 出于某种原因，至少在亚洲语境下，它似乎演变成了专门指代旅居海外的白人。我从没听过旅美华人被称为“外籍人士”，尽管过去十年在华人众多的北卡罗来纳州生活时，我曾努力去推广这种叫法。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: For some reason, people don't even talk about other East Asian people living in China as expats. It's a super loaded word. It's bothered me for a long time. I generally avoid it. But I don't avoid these expats.
transcript.zh: 不知道为什么，人们甚至也不会把在中国生活的其他东亚人称为“expat”。这是一个带有极强特定偏见的词，困扰我很久了，我通常会避开它。但我并不回避这些外籍朋友。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Now, to be sure, I lament the fact that any group of folks living abroad, in a place as interesting as Beijing especially, would choose only to spend their time with others like them, rather than participating meaningfully in the life of the city where they live. Their loss.
transcript.zh: 当然，如果任何一群旅居海外的人——尤其是在北京这样有趣的城市里——只愿意和自己的同类待在一起，而不去深度融入当地城市生活，我确实会感到遗憾。这是他们的损失。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: But honestly, I'm not one of those people. I try to divide my time and hang out a lot with my, my bandmates who are Beijingers, and with other people I know from the rock scene. I am not ashamed that I have lots of foreign friends here, too.
transcript.zh: 但坦白讲，我并不是那种人。我努力平衡自己的时间，经常和我的北京本地乐队队友混在一起，也会联系摇滚圈认识的其他朋友。不过，我在这里有很多外国朋友，这也完全没什么好羞愧的。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Foreigners living abroad in a city like Beijing are not to be shunned out of some notional commitment to authenticity. I know people who've been like that. "No way am I going to that party, it's all laowai," they'll say, you know, using a word for foreigners that's not entirely value-neutral.
transcript.zh: 生活在北京这种城市的外国人，绝不该因为某种虚幻的“纯粹本土情结”而被排斥。我认识不少人就是这种态度：“我才不去那个派对呢，全都是老外，”他们会这么说，用了“老外”这个并不完全中立的词。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And come on, this is especially silly given the sorts of foreigners who live long-term in Beijing. I rate them, for the most part, an amazing bunch. They live here very intentionally, making a real effort to connect with and understand the city and, and the country.
transcript.zh: 拜托，考虑到长期生活在北京的这群外国人是些什么样的人，这种态度就显得尤为荒谬了。在我看来，他们绝大多数都非常优秀。他们是非常自觉、有意识地选择生活在这里，真正努力去接触和理解这座城市，乃至这个国家。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: If, if, if they tend to gather occasionally at the same bars, at the same watering holes, I think that can be forgiven. They're eager, just as I am, you know, to share their observations, to float their various hypotheses, or sometimes just to talk about the books they're reading or the shows they're watching, or just to gossip.
transcript.zh: 如果他们偶尔喜欢聚在同一家酒吧、同一个据点，我觉得这也完全无可厚非。他们和我一样，热衷于分享自己的观察、探讨各自的假说，或者有时只是聊聊手头看的书、追的剧，甚至纯粹八卦一番。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So yeah, most of the people I happened across during the course of this weekend who were willing to have a mic stuck up in their face, and when it wasn't so loud that doing so would have been pointless, happened to have been foreign residents. They also happened to speak English, and as you may have noticed, this is an English-language show.
transcript.zh: 所以没错，这个周末我遇到的那些愿意让我把麦克风怼到脸前、且周围环境没吵到录不下去的人，恰好大都是外籍居民。他们也恰好都说英语，而正如各位所知，这是一档英文节目。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah, so this all still sounds more defensive than I wanted it to. The fact is, the kind of foreign community that a city draws to it says something meaningful about that city. I am grateful to be part of this community.
transcript.zh: 说了这么多，听起来还是比我预想的要更具防卫意味。但事实是：一座城市所吸引的外籍社群特质，在很大程度上能折射出这座城市本身的内涵。我很庆幸能成为这个社群的一份子。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: It gives the place something of a, a small town feel, where you keep running into the same bunch of folks and you kind of know the gossip. You see them navigating some of the same contradictions that you face, like one that I'll flick at during the little capsule conversations that follow.
transcript.zh: 它给这里增添了一种类似“小镇”的人情味，让你总能碰到同一拨熟人，彼此心照不宣地聊聊八卦。你会看到他们也在面对和你一样的种种矛盾，比如在接下来精选的小对话中，我就会轻轻带出其中的一个侧面。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So many of us were really drawn to Beijing and to China because of the incredible pace of change, and yet so many of us also feel nostalgia.
transcript.zh: 我们当中的很多人之所以深深被北京、被中国所吸引，是因为这里日新月异、令人难以置信的变革步伐；然而，我们当中同样有很多人，心中也满怀着对过去的乡愁与留恋。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: For the place that we initially encountered, you know, which we sailed past long ago already on this swift-moving river of time. So, I get a lot of emails, Twitter DMs, and especially LinkedIn messages of late that basically say, "Hey, I'm so-and-so, and I work at such-and-such, and I'm a longtime listener to your show. I'll be in Beijing from this date to that date, and would love to buy you a cup of coffee or a beer."
transcript.zh: 我们最初相遇的那个地方，在飞逝的时光长河中，其实早就已经被我们远远抛在身后了。所以，我最近收到了很多电子邮件、Twitter 私信，尤其是 LinkedIn 上的留言，大意都是：“嗨，我是某某某，在某某机构工作，是您节目的老听众了。我会在某月某日到某月某日之间来北京，非常想请您喝杯咖啡或喝杯啤酒。”

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Now, I am a gregarious fellow, and I love nothing more than meeting people with common interests or even, you know, without common interests. And I do like coffee and beer. So, having never seen a red flag thus far, touch wood, I've never said no.
transcript.zh: 我这个人向来好客爱交际，最喜欢结识志趣相投的朋友，甚至就算兴趣不同也没关系。而且我也确实喜欢咖啡和啤酒。所以，谢天谢地，迄今为止我还没遇到过什么不靠谱的人，因此从来没拒绝过。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: The first guy you'll hear from reached out basically like that. I didn't say his name very clearly on the recording, so I'm going to do it here. His name is Olumide Abimbola. We seriously vibed on all sorts of stuff—on books, on politics, on theories of development, on parenting and our parents.
transcript.zh: 你们将听到的第一位朋友，基本上就是通过这种方式联系上我的。在录音里我念他的名字念得不太清楚，所以我在这里重新介绍一下。他叫 Olumide Abimbola。我们在各种话题上都极具共鸣——聊书、聊政治、聊发展理论、聊育儿，以及我们的父母辈。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And we ended up spending like 5 hours together. 5 hours so well-spent. I learned, among other things, that Yoruba, his language, is also a tonal language. It has a kind of "do-re-mi" tonal system, so I think it's like "Olumide," but I'm probably getting that wrong. Anyway, here we are.
transcript.zh: 结果我们在一起聊了大概五个小时。那五个小时过得极其充实。除了其他收获之外，我还了解到他的母语约鲁巴语也是一种声调语言。它有一种类似“do-re-mi”的音调系统，所以我想发音大概是“Olumide”，但我很可能读得不对。不管怎样，我们开始吧。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So, it's Friday afternoon. I'm sitting in my favorite café, Café Zarah, on Guloudongdajie in central Beijing. This is where I tend to work most days of the week.
transcript.zh: 现在是周五下午。我正坐在我最喜欢的咖啡馆 Café Zarah 里，它位于北京老城区的鼓楼东大街。每周的大多数日子，我基本都会在这里办公。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And I've just been joined here by a new friend, somebody I met earlier, Olumide Abimbola, who comes from Abuja in Nigeria, but lives in Berlin now, where he runs a think tank. And he's not a "China guy" per se. He works on Germany and on issues of development in Africa, and naturally is interested in China. Is this your first time here?
transcript.zh: 刚和我坐在一起的是一位新朋友，也是我之前刚认识的 Olumide Abimbola。他来自尼日利亚的阿布贾，但目前定居柏林，在那里运营一家智库。他本身并不是所谓的“中国通”，主要研究德国以及非洲的发展议题，自然也对中国很感兴趣。这是你第一次来这里吗？

transcript.speaker: Olumide Abimbola
transcript.en: My second time.
transcript.zh: 第二次了。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Oh, your second time in China. And I met him earlier this week. You know, he's a listener to Eric and Cobus' show, and to Sinica, and he reached out. I was really curious to hear now—it's been now five days that he's been here—about mostly about what questions you have about China. What has puzzled or surprised you, and what are you interested in knowing?
transcript.zh: 哦，第二次来中国。我们是本周早些时候认识的。他是 Eric 和 Cobus 的播客节目以及 Sinica 的听众，主动联系了我。我现在非常好奇想听听——他在这里待了五天了——你对中国有哪些疑问？有什么让你感到困惑或惊讶的，你又对了解哪些事情感兴趣？

transcript.speaker: Olumide Abimbola
transcript.en: Thank you very much, Kaiser. What has puzzled me? I don't really have any puzzles specifically. I'm curious. I'm trying to understand.
transcript.zh: 非常感谢，Kaiser。有什么让我困惑的？其实说不上具体有什么困惑。我更多是好奇，想要去理解。

transcript.speaker: Olumide Abimbola
transcript.en: I'm trying to see what's next. I'm trying to know how China moves ahead with partnerships around the world, including with Europe, where I live, with Africa, where I work and what I work on. What topics are interesting for the Beijing government, but also what topics are interesting for businesses here, on both sides—so on the Africa side and also on the European side.
transcript.zh: 我想看看接下来的走向是什么。我想了解中国如何推进与世界各地的伙伴关系，包括我生活的欧洲，以及我工作所在和研究的非洲。不仅想知道中国官方对哪些议题感兴趣，也想了解这里的企业对什么感兴趣，这涵盖了双边视角——即非洲与欧洲两端。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: We had a really interesting conversation here last weekend.
transcript.zh: 上周末我们在这里进行了一场非常有趣的对话。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Where we talked mainly about Germany's response to this post-COVID surge in EV exports especially, but in in in industrial exports of all sorts. You're in Germany, you had an interesting sort of one-word response to this.
transcript.zh: 我们主要讨论了德国对后疫情时代中国出口激增的反应，尤其是新能源汽车出口，但也包括各类工业品出口。你在德国生活，对此给出了一个很有意思的一字回应。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I don't know if you're going to be too polite to say this on tape, but tell me what your general thoughts are now having been here for a little while, having sort of witnessed Beijing's industrial might on display and what are you thinking now?
transcript.zh: 我不知道你在录音里会不会太客气而不愿直说，但能不能告诉我，在这里待了一阵子、亲眼见证了北京展现的工业实力之后，你的总体想法是什么？你现在怎么看？

transcript.speaker: Olumide Abimbola
transcript.en: Okay. So first of all, to talk a bit about that industrial might that you talked about. So, I was in Baoding yesterday. I was at a solar manufacturing factory, and I found things that I didn't know existed.
transcript.zh: 好的。首先谈谈你提到的那种工业实力。我昨天去了保定，参观了一家光伏制造工厂，发现了一些我此前根本不知道存在的东西。

transcript.speaker: Olumide Abimbola
transcript.en: So, which was it's called BIPV, so building-integrated PV, photovoltaic, where you could have a building and have pictures on it, but underneath those pictures were actually solar cells, you know, solar. I mean, I'd never seen it, I'd never thought about it.
transcript.zh: 也就是所谓的 BIPV，即建筑光伏一体化。建筑外观上可以印着画作，但画作之下实际上都是太阳能电池。我从没见过这种技术，也从未想过，

transcript.speaker: Olumide Abimbola
transcript.en: I'd never I didn't have a way of of understanding it until I actually saw it and spoke to the manufacturers of it. So it's a lot happening here, some of which we don't even know about until we actually come in contact with it.
transcript.zh: 直到我亲眼看到并和制造商交流，我才真正理解它。所以这里正在发生很多事情，其中一些我们直到真正接触之前甚至根本一无所知。

transcript.speaker: Olumide Abimbola
transcript.en: So, yeah, back to your question about Europe's response, because it's not only Germany, it's also Europe, right? Germany happens to be the industrial powerhouse of Europe, so it's feeling the pinch of the export surge from China quite a bit.
transcript.zh: 回到你关于欧洲反应的问题，因为这不仅关乎德国，也关乎整个欧洲，对吧？德国恰好是欧洲的工业引擎，所以它相当切实地感受到了中国出口激增所带来的冲击。

transcript.speaker: Olumide Abimbola
transcript.en: What do I think about it? I'm still trying to figure out what to think about it because I can understand the way the Germans feel. I can understand the way Europeans feel about what they see happening to them.
transcript.zh: 我怎么看？我仍在试图理清自己的看法，因为我能理解德国人的感受，我也能理解欧洲人看着眼下发生在自己身上的变局时的感受。

transcript.speaker: Olumide Abimbola
transcript.en: I think it didn't have to happen this way. They didn't have to land where they are right now, and they don't have to stay where they are. My feeling is the Chinese side also probably understands where Germany is coming from, because it's not that hard to understand.
transcript.zh: 我认为事情本不必发展到这种地步。他们本不必落到今天的境地，也不必困守在现状中。我的感觉是，中国方面大概也理解德国的立场，因为这并不难理解。

transcript.speaker: Olumide Abimbola
transcript.en: What I wish would happen is that both sides negotiate something that gives both sides something. I think that's possible, but I think Europe would have to move just like China would have to move as well.
transcript.zh: 我希望看到的是双方通过谈判达成某种方案，让彼此都能有所收获。我认为这是可能的，但我认为欧洲必须做出调整，正如中国也必须做出调整一样。

transcript.speaker: Olumide Abimbola
transcript.en: I don't like it when it feels like it ends up at just complaining, like, 'We don't want this.' Yeah, it's okay not to want something, but what do you want? And do you think what you want can be acceptable to the other side?
transcript.zh: 我不喜欢那种最后沦为一味抱怨的局面，比如‘我们不想要这个’。没错，不想要某样东西很正常，但你到底想要什么？而且你觉得你想要的能被对方接受吗？

transcript.speaker: Olumide Abimbola
transcript.en: I think that's where we need to get to, where we have things that both sides agree on that works for both of them.
transcript.zh: 我认为这才是我们需要达到的目标——找到双方都能认同、且对彼此都行之有效的方案。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So, that was Olumide, and we'll be hopefully having him on the show for a proper sit-down interview after a while.
transcript.zh: 刚才那是 Olumide。希望过段时间我们能邀请他来节目做一次正式的坐谈专访。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I spent the rest of that afternoon reading the book How Africa Works by Joe Studwell in preparation for an interview with him for the show later this week, and that'll be out in a couple of weeks.
transcript.zh: 那天下午剩下的时间，我都在读 Joe Studwell 的《How Africa Works》，为本周晚些时候对他的节目录制做准备，那期节目将在几周后上线。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I put in an hour of guitar exercises. I went home to do that, which I try to get those in daily. Then, I headed over to the new...
transcript.zh: 我练了一个小时吉他，专门回家练的，我尽量每天都坚持练琴。之后，我动身前往了新……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: ...rental near Tuanjiehu, where Fanfan had spent the afternoon cleaning up and getting the place ready for move-in day, which I look forward to. My daughter joined us there when she got off work, and we all headed to dinner at a place right by our new building, right basically at the foot of it.
transcript.zh: ……团结湖附近租的房子，凡凡整个下午都在那里打扫收拾，为搬家日做准备，对此我非常期待。我女儿下班后也赶过来和我们会合，我们一起去新楼旁边、基本就在楼底下的一家餐馆吃晚饭。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: It's called Meizhou Dongpo, a well-known Sichuan restaurant chain in Beijing, and this place has been there since 1997. It's actually the second branch to open in Beijing, after the one over by the Sino-Japanese Friendship Hospital, where I used to eat all the time.
transcript.zh: 餐馆叫眉州东坡，是北京一家著名的川菜连锁店，这家分店从1997年就开在那里了。它其实是北京开的第二家分店，仅次于中日友好医院旁边的那家，我以前经常去那里吃。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: We explored the neighborhood a bit until about, what, like 8:30, and then I headed over to, well, you will see.
transcript.zh: 我们在附近逛了逛，直到大概八点半左右，然后我动身前往——好吧，一会儿你们就知道了。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Okay, so I am at my favorite watering hole, as many listeners know, the Golden Weasel here on Dongsi Beidajie. And things are just getting started. It's about 9:00, and not many people have rolled in, but one guy, a good friend of mine named Michael Cherney, is here.
transcript.zh: 好了，我现在到了我最常去的那家心头好酒吧——许多听众都知道——位于东四北大街的“金鼬”（The Golden Weasel）。场子才刚刚热起来，现在大概九点，还没来多少人，不过有一位我的好朋友Michael Cherney已经到了。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Michael, I may have talked about his work before on the show, in fact I think I have. He's an amazing calligrapher, a painter, he does multimedia stuff, also a guitar player, and we have enjoyed many an evening here just sort of strumming on guitars.
transcript.zh: 关于Michael，我以前可能在节目里提到过他的作品，事实上我觉得我提过。他是一位令人惊叹的书法家、画家，从事多媒体创作，同时也是一名吉他手，我们曾在这里度过了许多个弹弹吉他的惬意夜晚。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Michael, what's on your mind these days? What are you thinking about when it comes to China of late?
transcript.zh: Michael，你最近在关注些什么？谈到最近的中国，你有什么想法？

transcript.speaker: Michael Cherney
transcript.en: There's a little bit of a hint of people coming back a little bit more than they used to, and so that is very encouraging. I think people are not buying into a lot of the negative hype as much as they used to. And so that's what we need.
transcript.zh: 隐约能感觉到，回来的人似乎比以前多了一些，这非常令人鼓舞。我觉得大家不再像过去那样容易被负面炒作所左右了。而这正是我们所需要的。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah, for sure. So, help me scene-set here. What does the Golden Weasel mean to you, besides, you know, good Scotch and good times?
transcript.zh: 确实如此。来帮我交代一下这里的背景吧。除了上好的苏格兰威士忌和欢乐时光，金鼬酒吧对你而言意味着什么？

transcript.speaker: Michael Cherney
transcript.en: I actually only started to come fairly recently. You know, Anthony is in the softball league. We have our Beijing, very low-pressure, co-ed slow-pitch softball league.
transcript.zh: 其实我也是不久前才常来的。Anthony在垒球联盟里，我们在北京有一个氛围非常轻松的男女混合慢投垒球联盟。

transcript.speaker: Michael Cherney
transcript.en: And so, I would hear about people stopping by here, you know, for years. It actually changed locations not that long ago, and so, and it's close to home, and so I quickly became addicted.
transcript.zh: 好多年来我都一直听人说会顺道来这里喝一杯。它不久前其实换了地址，而且离我家很近，所以我很快就上瘾了。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: It's a great place. I come here often enough that I've met many of the people who frequent the place, and it's invariable that I come here and end up in good conversations with interesting people.
transcript.zh: 这是个很棒的地方。我经常来这儿，常客里的大多数我都认识了；每次过来，无一例外都能和有趣的人聊上几句好天。

transcript.speaker: Michael Cherney
transcript.en: Yeah, and you know, it also seems as if the people wanting to express themselves, either through music or poetry, or that—I know it was a little bit challenging for a little while, but it seems to, it seems to be a little bit better recently.
transcript.zh: 是的，而且感觉那些想通过音乐、诗歌等方式来表达自我的人——我知道前阵子确实有些困难，但最近似乎好转了一些。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah, and may it continue to flourish. So, the owner, or one of the two co-owners of the Golden Weasel just walked in, Anthony Tao. You've heard him on the show before if you've been a longtime listener.
transcript.zh: 是的，愿它继续欣欣向荣。金鼬酒吧的老板，或者说是两位合伙人之一，Anthony Tao刚刚进来了。如果是老听众的话，你们以前在节目里听过他的声音。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: He was my colleague for many years at The China Project. He was the managing editor there, and of course he is...
transcript.zh: 他在The China Project和我共事多年，曾在那儿担任执行主编，当然他也是……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: A well-known poet, the poet laureate of Beijing. I interviewed him about his poetry collection. We met in Beijing sometime ago. Anthony, how are you, man?
transcript.zh: 一位著名的诗人，堪称北京的桂冠诗人。前段时间我们在北京碰面时，我还就他的诗集做过专访。Anthony，最近怎么样，哥们儿？

transcript.speaker: Anthony Tao
transcript.en: Doing fantastic. Even better now that I am having some of this Bruichladdich that you brought in, the Micro-Provenance. Do you know why they call it this?
transcript.zh: 挺好的。尤其是现在喝上了你带来的这款布赫拉迪（Bruichladdich）微产区系列（Micro-Provenance），感觉更棒了。你知道他们为什么叫这个名字吗？

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I do not, no. Tell me. I mean, because it's a tiny batch. It's a single barrel, and it's actually got a lot number on it, and I think there's only some finite number of bottles.
transcript.zh: 我还真不知道，给我讲讲。我的理解是，因为它是小批量、单桶装瓶，瓶身还标了批次号，而且数量非常有限。

transcript.speaker: Anthony Tao
transcript.en: Well, you know terroir is a huge concept in wine and always has been, but hasn't been a thing in whiskey at all. But there's a person that was associated with Bruichladdich—I don't actually know if he's still there. I think he's since moved on, but he was determined to prove that terroir matters in whiskey, in where you grow the barley, the soil conditions, etc. And so, it started as an experiment on some of their plots.
transcript.zh: 你知道，“风土”（Terroir）在葡萄酒界一直是个极其重要的概念，但在威士忌领域过去根本没有这一说。布赫拉迪有一位元老——我不知道他现在还在不在，应该已经离开去其他地方了——他当时下定决心要证明风土对威士忌同样至关重要，比如大麦的种植地、土壤条件等等。于是，这最初是在他们部分地块上展开的一场试验。

transcript.speaker: Anthony Tao
transcript.en: And this series, I believe, arose out of that where you can... They had this line of whiskies as well called... Oh, sorry, interrupted by a customer here. It's not their... Oh, shoot. Now I need to look it up.
transcript.zh: 据我所知，这个系列就是由此诞生的……他们当时还推出过一条产品线叫……不好意思，来客人了先应酬一下。不是他们的……糟糕，我现在得查一下名字了。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Well, don't worry about it. Yeah, the Port Charlotte's good. I've had that, but this is a Bruichladdich Micro-Provenance single cask and it's unbelievable. I just opened it.
transcript.zh: 没事，不用纠结。夏洛特港（Port Charlotte）确实很棒，我喝过。但这是布赫拉迪微产区单桶，味道简直绝了。我才刚开瓶。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I bought this in Singapore on my way back from Indonesia at the duty-free there, and my wife has now become accustomed to me bringing back a bottle from everywhere I go. So, I've got quite the collection going. So listen, Tao, tell me about the Golden Weasel. Tell me about your vision for the place, what you think the role that it plays here in the community, and tell me a little bit about... Well, tell me what's been on your mind. What's something that's become clear to you recently?
transcript.zh: 这是我从印尼回程途经新加坡时，在当地免税店买的。我妻子现在已经习惯我每到一个地方就带瓶酒回来了，不知不觉我都快攒成收藏了。对了Tao，跟我聊聊黄鼠狼酒吧（Golden Weasel）吧。谈谈你对这家店的设想，你觉得它在本地社群中扮演了怎样的角色？还有……聊聊你最近都在琢磨些什么，最近有什么想通的事吗？

transcript.speaker: Anthony Tao
transcript.en: The entire reason for the space existing is to provide people a dependable space for meeting up, for talking about whatever's on their mind. You know, we take this for granted that this is actually what bars and cafes originally were supposed to do. It's this idea of a third space.
transcript.zh: 这个空间存在的全部意义，就是给人们提供一个可靠的聚脚点，让大家能碰碰头，聊聊彼此心里所想的事。其实我们常常把这视为理所当然，但最初的酒吧和咖啡馆本就是干这个的，这就是所谓的‘第三空间’理念。

transcript.speaker: Anthony Tao
transcript.en: Most importantly, a place that you can dependably find some friends or people with similar values, where they can gather, they can meet, strengthen bonds, and create new ones.
transcript.zh: 最重要的是，这是一个只要你来，就笃定能遇到朋友或价值观相近之人的地方。大家聚在这里彼此相见，既能巩固老交情，也能结识新朋友。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah, I can say I've never failed to come here of an evening and not get into a really fun, interesting conversation, and meet...
transcript.zh: 是啊，就我个人而言，每次晚上来这儿，无一例外都能聊上几场格外有趣、尽兴的话题，而且还能结识……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: People doing cool things here. So, now, what is something that has become clear to you recently, Anthony?
transcript.zh: 大家都在这里做着很酷的事。那么，Anthony，最近有什么事情让你想明白了？

transcript.speaker: Anthony Tao
transcript.en: A tough question, but I think our ability, any individual's ability to paint a complete picture is insufficient. We are unable to.
transcript.zh: 这个问题挺难回答的，但我觉得，我们或者说任何一个个体，想要勾勒出一幅全貌的能力都是不够的。我们根本做不到。

transcript.speaker: Anthony Tao
transcript.en: Our language is not enough. Our ideas aren't enough. The moment we talk about something, we create... and very specifically, I want to make clear I'm talking about, the example I have in mind is talking about issues about China.
transcript.zh: 我们的语言词不达意，思想也不够全面。一旦我们开口去谈论某件事，我们就会制造……具体来说，我想澄清的是，我脑海中想到的例子正是讨论关于中国的问题。

transcript.speaker: Anthony Tao
transcript.en: The Mbappé situation, for instance, recently. The moment you express an idea, you vocalize it, you put it out there, and then you create these opportunities for all these counterpoints immediately.
transcript.zh: 比如最近姆巴佩的那起争议事件。只要你一表达某种观点，把它说出口、公之于众，立刻就会招致各种反驳的声音。

transcript.speaker: Anthony Tao
transcript.en: It's like a variant of Schrödinger's cat, right? You can know position, but not wave function. It's like in China, you can talk about this one opinion, and you're talking about that, and yet the moment you say it, everyone else will think about something else. They'll steer the conversation elsewhere.
transcript.zh: 这就像是薛定谔的猫的一个变体，对吧？你可以知道位置，但无法确定波函数。在中国也是这样，你可以提出某一个观点，你专注在这一点上，然而只要你说出来，其他人就会联想到别的东西，把话题引向其他方向。

transcript.speaker: Anthony Tao
transcript.en: You might have in your mind a very full grasp of a situation. You might see every single angle. You might see why this controversy started, why some people are offended, why people think it's stupid, why it actually is silly, and yet why it's also important, all the historical context, etc. But you can never actually express that.
transcript.zh: 你在自己脑海里可能对局势有着极为全面的把握，能看清每一个角度。你明白这场争议因何而起，为什么有人感到被冒犯，为什么有人觉得它愚蠢，为什么它本身确实很荒谬、但同时又为何非常重要，以及所有的历史背景等等。但你永远无法把这些完整表达出来。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: You're absolutely right, and I've seen people try and fail and get dunked on viciously on Twitter. That's why I have not said a goddamned word on it, and I still won't.
transcript.zh: 你说得太对了，我亲眼见过有人试图去解释却以失败告终，还在 Twitter 上被骂得体无完肤。这就是为什么我对这件事只字不提，而且依然不会置评。

transcript.speaker: Michael Cherney
transcript.en: Schrödinger's Máo instead of Māo.
transcript.zh: 不是薛定谔的“猫”，是薛定谔的“毛”。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Schrödinger's Máo! That's a good one. Was that Michael?
transcript.zh: 薛定谔的“毛”！这个谐音梗太棒了。刚才是 Michael 说的吗？

transcript.speaker: Michael Cherney
transcript.en: I said Schrödinger's Máo instead of Schrödinger's Māo.
transcript.zh: 我说的是薛定谔的“毛”，而不是薛定谔的“猫”。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah, that's the thing with these bilingual puns. There's like a handful of people in the world who would appreciate Michael Cherney's 'Schrödinger's Máo.' I've found that Chinese people don't really dig puns that involve what would be a homophone except for the tone. They make sense to foreigners for whom the tone is sort of not so integral. But anyway.
transcript.zh: 是啊，这种双语谐音梗就是这样。全世界大概只有极少数人能领会 Michael Cherney 这个“薛定谔的毛”的笑点。我发现中国人其实不太感冒那种除了声调不同、其他都同音的谐音梗。对外国人来说这种梗反而行得通，因为声调对他们而言没那么不可或缺。但不管怎么说吧。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So, māo, first tone, meaning cat, and máo, second tone, is the surname, of course, of the late Chairman, in the news again, of course, because of this whole kerfuffle over Mbappé. But yeah, we get it.
transcript.zh: 所以，第一声的“猫”意思是猫，而第二声的“毛”当然是已故主席的姓氏。因为姆巴佩引发的这场轩然大波，这个名字最近又上了新闻。不过没错，我们都懂这个梗。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So, this is Amy, and Amy's from Minnesota, and...
transcript.zh: 这位是 Amy，Amy 来自明尼苏达州，还有……

transcript.speaker: Amy
transcript.en: Oh, don'tcha know!
transcript.zh: 哎呀，这谁不知道呢！

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So I'm just talking to people about... this is a Beijing weekend edition, and just talking to people about what life is like here as an expat living in Beijing these days, and what especially the Golden Weasel means to you.
transcript.zh: 我正在和大家聊聊……这是一期北京周末特别节目，就是和大家聊聊如今作为一个在京生活的外国人，这里的日子过得怎么样，尤其是金鼬酒吧对你而言意味着什么。

transcript.speaker: Amy
transcript.en: What is the Golden...
transcript.zh: 金鼬对我来说……

transcript.speaker: Amy
transcript.en: What does the Weasel mean to me? You know, Anthony and Dan had a different name for the Golden Weasel, and I told them to pick that name. I forgot what it is now. They chose Golden Weasel, I feel like, to spite me. And it worked out.
transcript.zh: 黄鼠狼酒吧对我来说意味着什么？你知道，Anthony 和 Dan 最初给黄鼠狼酒吧起了另一个名字，我当时还叫他们就用那个名字。我现在忘了叫什么了。我觉得他们选“黄鼠狼”这个名字，纯粹是为了气我。不过效果还挺好。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Do you feel spited?
transcript.zh: 你觉得被气到了吗？

transcript.speaker: Amy
transcript.en: I always feel spited by Anthony. But he is my dear, close friend of almost 15 years. So the Golden Weasel means a lot to me because, uh, Anthony has been my spiteful friend for 15 years.
transcript.zh: 我总觉得被 Anthony 气到。但他是我认识快15年的挚友。所以黄鼠狼酒吧对我意义重大，因为 Anthony 已经当了我15年爱跟我对着干的朋友。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: What's been on your mind when it comes to China recently? What have you been thinking about?
transcript.zh: 最近关于中国，你脑子里都在想些什么？你一直在琢磨什么呢？

transcript.speaker: Amy
transcript.en: Oh, um... China, just like, I've been here for almost 15 years. And the thing that's on my mind always is just like, how can we keep the vibes going, you know?
transcript.zh: 哦……嗯……关于中国，我在这里生活了快15年了。我脑子里一直在想的其实是：我们该怎么保持住这种氛围，你懂吗？

transcript.speaker: Amy
transcript.en: Like, I'd say Beijing 2012 was really like a peak for me. And I don't know if that's because like that's my first year in China, everything was new and exciting.
transcript.zh: 比如，我觉得2012年的北京对我来说算是个巅峰期。我不知道是不是因为那是我来中国的第一年，一切都既新鲜又令人兴奋。

transcript.speaker: Amy
transcript.en: And like there were a lot of cool concerts happening, like a lot of like vibes. But I feel like the vibes have changed over the years, but we've found a way to like manage to still live this cool expat lifestyle, despite all the changes and all the, you know, challenges.
transcript.zh: 那时有很多很酷的演出，很有气氛。但我觉得这些年来那种氛围变了，可无论经历了多少变化和各种挑战，我们还是想办法保持住了这种很酷的在华外籍人士生活方式。

transcript.speaker: Amy
transcript.en: Even COVID, even like the 'brickening', everything. And we've still found a way. And it's amazing that the Golden Weasel is this place that is like this beacon for all of us.
transcript.zh: 即使经历疫情，经历了“封墙打洞”，经历了所有这一切。我们依然找到了自己的方式。令人惊喜的是，黄鼠狼酒吧成了这样一个地方，就像是照亮我们所有人的灯塔。

transcript.speaker: Amy
transcript.en: I don't know what to do on a Friday night, just go to the Weasel, I will know somebody. And that's the vibe I always had in 2012. That's the vibe I still have now. It has taken all of us to make sure that that continues.
transcript.zh: 如果周五晚上不知道去哪儿，直接去黄鼠狼就行，肯定能碰上熟人。这正是2012年我常常感受到的氛围，也是我如今依然能感受到的氛围。要延续这种感觉，需要我们所有人的共同努力。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Fantastic. Thanks, Amy.
transcript.zh: 太棒了。谢谢你，Amy。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So the 'brickening' that Amy referred to was an effort by the Beijing city government—actually, I don't know whether it was the municipality or individual district governments. But anyway, an effort to tidy up the streets by bricking over illegal or semi-legal storefronts that individual homeowners had opened up onto the streets, onto the hutongs, where they were, you know, selling snacks or drinks or cigarettes, and even occasionally operating kind of big retail concerns.
transcript.zh: Amy 提到的“封墙打洞整治”，是北京市政府——其实我也不太确定是市级还是各区政府——为了整治市容开展的一项行动，即把居民私自在临街或胡同里破墙开办的违法或半违规商铺用砖封上。这些小店往往兜售零食、饮料、香烟，偶尔甚至还会经营规模不小的零售店面。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: It was happening around the time that we left, my family left for North Carolina back in 2016, and it continued into the next year as I understand it. It was funny how people continued to sell stuff out of the windows that hadn't been bricked over.
transcript.zh: 这大致发生在我们离开的时候——我和家人在2016年回了北卡罗来纳州——据我所知，整治一直持续到了第二年。有趣的是，人们后来开始通过还没被砖封死的窗户继续对外卖东西。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Okay, so it's Saturday now. I spent the first half of the day basically sitting in a China Unicom business office to arrange for installation of my new fiber-to-the-premises service in the apartment that my wife and I just rented in Tuanjiehu, which is a great neighborhood. But...
transcript.zh: 好了，现在是周六。大半天时间我基本上都耗在中国联通的营业厅里，为我和妻子刚刚在团结湖租下的公寓办理光纤入户宽带的安装手续。那是个很棒的街区，不过……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Here I am. I almost forgot that I had this commitment to speak at this conference here at the HKU's Talent Forum. And I just ran into my good friend who you've heard on the show before, Wang Zichen. Say hi, Wang Zichen.
transcript.zh: 我到了。我差点忘了自己还要在港大举办的这个人才论坛上发言。我正好碰到了我的好友 Wang Zichen，大家以前也在节目里听过他的声音。Wang Zichen，打个招呼吧。

transcript.speaker: Wang Zichen
transcript.en: Hi, good to see you here. Glad you remembered you should speak at the, towards the end of the forum, huh?
transcript.zh: 嗨，很高兴在这儿见到你。真庆幸你还记得论坛快结束的时候你得发言，哈哈。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: What's going on? How have you been? What's going on here this weekend at the forum?
transcript.zh: 最近怎么样？过得好吗？这个周末论坛这儿都在探讨些什么？

transcript.speaker: Wang Zichen
transcript.en: Well, it's my first time to be in this Beijing center of the University of Hong Kong. And I think they're putting on a very good forum. They've had senior professors, not just from the University of Hong Kong, but also Tsinghua University, and coming here to share their latest research in a more accessible manner to laypeople like me.
transcript.zh: 这是我第一次来香港大学的北京中心。我觉得他们这次论坛办得很不错。他们请来了资深教授，不仅有港大的，还有清华大学的，他们在这里以一种更加深入浅出的方式向我这样的外行分享最新的研究成果。

transcript.speaker: Wang Zichen
transcript.en: But also debating the crucial changes like AI and how universities, how education systems should adapt to these changes. These are, of course, profound questions. What's your obligation?
transcript.zh: 他们还在探讨人工智能等关键变革，以及大学和教育体系应该如何适应这些变化。这些当然都是非常深刻的议题。那你这次的任务是什么？

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: My obligation appears to be to be on a panel in which I will be trying to talk about how technology, especially AI, might advance people-to-people relations or understanding of the humanities or scientific and cultural exchange.
transcript.zh: 我的任务似乎是参加一个小组讨论，我得尝试聊聊技术，特别是人工智能，如何推动民间交流、促进对人文科学的理解，或者助力科技与文化交流。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Which is, it's going to be weird because, really, all I see is securitization of the technology and division of it. But I'm going to be at the Golden Weasel tonight. Are you going to come along?
transcript.zh: 这其实挺尴尬的，因为说实话，我看到的尽是技术的泛安全化与随之而来的分裂。不过，我今晚会去 Golden Weasel 酒吧，你要一起来吗？

transcript.speaker: Wang Zichen
transcript.en: Probably not. I'm a little bit deprived of my sleep, so, yeah.
transcript.zh: 大概去不了，我最近有点缺觉，所以算了。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Okay. Well, get a good night's sleep.
transcript.zh: 行吧，那好好睡一觉。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Okay, so the guy who invited me to speak at this forum is Wang Feng. He's the former editor of the Chinese edition of the Financial Times, a former Caixin journalist, a really well-regarded journalist here, and always one of the people I turned to for just good sense on China.
transcript.zh: 好的，邀请我来这个论坛发言的人是 Wang Feng。他是《金融时报》中文网的前主编，也曾是《财新》的记者，在这边是一位备受尊敬的媒体人，也是在看待中国问题上我经常去请教、极具真知灼见的人之一。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I don't know how it is that you've not been on Sinica before, but we need to get you on. Tell me about this forum and what you're doing up here this weekend.
transcript.zh: 我真不知道你怎么之前一直没上过 Sinica，我们得找个时间录一期。跟我讲讲这个论坛吧，你这个周末在这儿忙些什么呢？

transcript.speaker: Wang Feng
transcript.en: Right. The University of Hong Kong is throwing this talent forum in Beijing, bringing our vice presidents, our star professors, and also a lot of local top academics, scientists, basically to sell our top-notch graduates.
transcript.zh: 好的。香港大学在北京举办了这个人才论坛，把我们的副校长、明星教授，以及许多本地的顶尖学者和科学家都请了过来，基本上就是来推销我们的顶尖毕业生的。

transcript.speaker: Wang Feng
transcript.en: Because the University of Hong Kong's Asia's number one, but up here in Beijing, with Beida and Tsinghua, Renda, all of those ruling the sky, we don't really have a very high profile.
transcript.zh: 因为虽然港大在亚洲名列前茅，但来到北京，有北大、清华、人大这些名校遮天蔽日，我们的知名度其实并没有那么高。

transcript.speaker: Wang Feng
transcript.en: This is what we're doing. We're bringing all of our biggest guns here to sell our top graduates, to help them get better jobs. That's what we do.
transcript.zh: 这就是我们在做的事。我们倾尽全力派出最强阵容，就是为了推介我们的优秀毕业生，帮他们找到更好的工作。这就是我们的目的。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So you gave up a role as editor-in-chief of the Chinese edition of the FT, which is a very prestigious job, to do what at HKU now? What are you doing? What's your...
transcript.zh: 这么说，你放弃了《金融时报》中文网总编辑这样一份声望极高的工作，跑到港大去干什么了？你现在具体在做什么？你的职责是……

transcript.speaker: Wang Feng
transcript.en: To do PR for the university.
transcript.zh: 就是给大学做公关传播。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Gone to the dark side, huh?
transcript.zh: 跳到对立面去了是吧，哈哈。

transcript.speaker: Wang Feng
transcript.en: Oh, yes, but not so dark. I mean, I work with scientists and young students. That's what I love.
transcript.zh: 哈哈，算是吧，但也没那么糟。我是说，能跟科学家和年轻学生打交道，这正是我热爱的工作。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah. I mean, and you're perfect for...
transcript.zh: 是啊，完全能理解。而且这份工作对你来说再合适不过了……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: For this job, I mean, such a good communicator. And thank you for inviting me. And I'm sorry, I'm about to disappoint you because I'm not going to have anything smart to say, but I will do my best.
transcript.zh: 这份工作，他真的是个出色的沟通者。非常感谢你的邀请。不过很抱歉，我可能要让你失望了，因为我接下来恐怕说不出什么高见，但我会尽力而为。

transcript.speaker: Wang Feng
transcript.en: Well, our audience will love you. As you see, so many of them are already your fans.
transcript.zh: 哎呀，我们的听众绝对会喜欢你的。你看，台下已经有那么多人是你的粉丝了。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Oh, well, for the weird reasons. I just had this woman come up to me and say, "I hear that you're a famous rock star. Can I have your WeChat?" And the guy next to me said, "Do you even know what band he was in? Have you ever heard of Tang Dynasty?" "No." So...
transcript.zh: 啊，好吧，原因千奇百怪。刚才就有位女士走过来对我说：“听说您曾是个著名的摇滚明星，能加个微信吗？”旁边那哥们儿就问她：“你甚至知道他是在哪个乐队吗？你听过唐朝乐队吗？”她说：“没有。”所以……

transcript.speaker: Wang Feng
transcript.en: Right, but your recent interviews with Hou Lang, those were really impressive. I love that you connect so well with the younger generation.
transcript.zh: 对，但你最近和《后浪》做的那些采访，真的非常精彩。我很赞赏你能和年轻一代建立起如此深入的共鸣。

transcript.speaker: Wang Feng
transcript.en: And these guys, these young girls, young guys, they're so interested in pop culture 30, 20 years ago. That's so interesting, the cross-generational cultural infusion.
transcript.zh: 而且这些年轻人，不管是年轻女孩还是小伙子，竟然对二三十年前的流行文化那么感兴趣。这种跨世代的文化交融，真是太有意思了。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah, it's really sad. I always have somebody come up to me after I'm done speaking, the young person will always say, "郭老师，我父母是听您的音乐长大的。" And what's wrong with that?
transcript.zh: 是啊，其实挺让人感慨的。每次我讲完，总会有年轻人跑过来跟我说：“郭老师，我父母是听您的音乐长大的。”这有什么不妥吗？

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So, surprisingly, that didn't go too badly. It was actually okay. I got up, and in spite of the fact that I could barely hear, in fact, I couldn't really hear, I had to sort of read lips to hear what the moderator was asking me.
transcript.zh: 出人意料的是，那场活动进行得并不差。其实挺顺利的。我走上台，尽管我几乎听不见——说实话，我确实完全听不清，基本得靠读唇语来明白主持人在问我什么。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I used my self-introduction section to apologize that I was going to speak English. I said it in Chinese, but that I was going to speak English because I had a stilted vocabulary and wouldn't be able to express myself well. So I spoke English, but it was good.
transcript.zh: 我在自我介绍环节先道了个歉，解释说我得用英语发言。我是用中文说明这一点的，但表示因为自己中文词汇生硬匮乏，无法充分表达思想，所以还是讲英文。不过效果挺好。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And you know, I was asked about what technology can do to sort of bridge the gap between peoples of different cultures and different backgrounds. And I talked a little bit about, you know, some of the historical cases where it did.
transcript.zh: 当时有人问我，技术能在弥合不同文化、不同背景的人群之间的鸿沟方面发挥怎样的作用。我就谈了谈历史上通过技术实现沟通的一些具体案例。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I talked about the Republic of Letters in the 17th and 18th century, and all the scientific communication between the different natural philosophers all over Europe in their common language, Latin.
transcript.zh: 我提到了17和18世纪的“文人共和国”（Republic of Letters），以及全欧洲的自然哲学家们如何利用拉丁语这一共通语言进行广泛的科学交流。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And then I talked about—this is why I couldn't say it in Chinese—it's the Committee on Scholarly Communication with the People's Republic of China, the CSCPRC, and the important role that it played after the Nixon opening in sort of re-establishing scientific communications with China.
transcript.zh: 接着我还谈到了——这也是为什么我没法用中文说——美中学术交流委员会（CSCPRC），以及它在尼克松破冰访华后，为重建与中国的科学交流所发挥的重要作用。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: It's always been a subject of interest for me. And talked about, you know, how today, in this age of weaponized interdependence, there is so much mistrust and there is suspicion of any scientific collaboration.
transcript.zh: 这一直是我非常感兴趣的课题。我还谈到，在当今这种“武器化相互依存”的时代，彼此间充斥着不信任，任何科学合作都会遭到质疑。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And how, despite the fact that I still see a lot of papers that are clearly co-authored by people whose names are spelled in pinyin with obviously people of European backgrounds and other backgrounds...
transcript.zh: 虽然我依然能看到大量论文是由明显拼写为中文拼音的学者与具有欧洲及其他背景的学者共同合著的，但如今的情况依然令人担忧……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: This is, you know, this is under threat. Um, yeah, it turned out okay. Anyway, I am about to meet up with a group of friends who are variously in town. Chris White from Columbus, from the Ohio State University, Andy Rothman, and my friend Graham Webster. So it's going to be a good group, it'll be fun, and I will talk to them as we go.
transcript.zh: 这正面临威胁。嗯，效果还不错。不管怎样，我马上要去见几位正好都在城里的朋友。有来自俄亥俄州立大学的 Chris White、Andy Rothman，还有我的朋友 Graham Webster。这会是一个很棒的局，肯定很有趣，稍后我会边聊边录。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Okay, so we're about to go to dinner and a couple of the guys who I'm having dinner with have just shown up. One of them is the well-known Andy Rothman, who has been of course a guest on the show before. Andy is, by my lights, just one of the people who gets the Chinese economy best.
transcript.zh: 好的，我们正准备去吃晚饭，跟我一起吃晚饭的几位刚到。其中一位就是大家非常熟悉的 Andy Rothman，他之前当然也做客过我们的节目。在我看来，Andy 绝对是对中国经济理解最深刻的人之一。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So, I know you were here for three weeks not too terribly long ago, but you just rolled into town last night. What are you most anxious to find out on this trip?
transcript.zh: 所以，我知道你不久前才在这里待了三周，但你昨晚又刚回到北京。这趟行程你最渴望了解些什么？

transcript.speaker: Andy Rothman
transcript.en: Mostly I just miss the food. Can we talk about that? But from an economics perspective, I'm trying to figure out why the government is not as nervous as I am about the continuing slowdown in income growth and consumption.
transcript.zh: 其实我主要是想念这里的美食，能先聊聊这个吗？不过从经济学角度来看，我正试图弄明白，对于收入增长和消费的持续放缓，为什么政府似乎没有像我这么担忧。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Okay, that's been on a lot of people's minds. These days it's become fashionable to describe the Chinese economy as K-shaped, and depending on whether you're on the upward-sloping arm or the downward-sloping arm, you have a very different perspective. Do you think that's an apt description?
transcript.zh: 好，这也是很多人都在思考的问题。近来把中国经济描述为“K型走势”蔚然成风，而且取决于你是处于上行分支还是下行分支，你的视角会截然不同。你认为这是一个贴切的描述吗？

transcript.speaker: Andy Rothman
transcript.en: Yes, I think we're also seeing something similar in the United States. So I spent two weeks in Shanghai about a month ago, and spent a lot of time talking to people in the tech sector, and they're all feeling really good. But everybody else, less so.
transcript.zh: 是的，我觉得在美国也出现了类似的状况。大约一个月前我在上海待了两周，花了很多时间跟科技界的人交流，他们感觉都非常好。但对于其他所有人来说，就没那么乐观了。

transcript.speaker: Andy Rothman
transcript.en: But I also spent a couple of days in Foshan, a city in Guangdong that I'm sure you're familiar with, but a lot of your listeners probably haven't heard of. It's a population of the size of Chicago, but just goes to show you how many big cities there are in China that people haven't heard of.
transcript.zh: 不过我还在广东佛山待了几天，我相信你很熟悉这座城市，但很多听众可能没听说过。它的人口规模相当于芝加哥，这恰恰说明了中国有多少鲜为人知的大城市。

transcript.speaker: Andy Rothman
transcript.en: And I went there because it has been really hit hard by the property slowdown. Home sales are down on a square meter basis about 80% from the peak, and they also produce a lot of furniture and home appliances, so I wanted to see how that was doing.
transcript.zh: 我之所以去那里，是因为它受到了房地产下行的沉重打击。按建筑面积计算，其商品房销售额较峰值下跌了约80%；此外，佛山还生产大量的家具和家电，所以我想看看当地产业的情况。

transcript.speaker: Andy Rothman
transcript.en: Not great, but to me it's kind of symbolic of the resilience of Chinese entrepreneurs. Not great, but toughening it out.
transcript.zh: 虽然不太景气，但对我来说，这某种程度上象征着中国企业家的韧性。日子不好过，但都在咬牙硬扛。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Foshan, for those of you who don't know it, is the home furnishings capital of the world. Basically if you want ceiling fans, or floor tiles, or aluminum siding, or anything at all in the building trade, to furnish the interior of a home mainly, it's all made and sold, you know, in and around Foshan.
transcript.zh: 对于不了解佛山的朋友，它是世界家居用品之都。基本上如果你想要吊扇、地砖、铝制外墙护墙板，或者建筑装潢行业所需的任何材料——主要是用来装修室内空间的——全都是在佛山及周边地区生产和销售的。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I have a friend, a former journalist, who had a house she was fitting out in Germany. She made a trip especially to Foshan just to walk through these warehouses and say, 'this, this, this, this, and this.' Pretty amazing.
transcript.zh: 我有个曾做过记者的朋友，当时正在德国装修房子。她专门跑了一趟佛山，就是为了逛这些大仓库，然后一路指着说：‘这个、这个、这个，还有这个’，真是叹为观止。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Anyway, so how long are you in town for this time, Andy?
transcript.zh: 不管怎么说，Andy，你这次在北京待多久？

transcript.speaker: Andy Rothman
transcript.en: A week.
transcript.zh: 一周。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And what are we going to eat tonight?
transcript.zh: 那我们今晚去吃什么？

transcript.speaker: Andy Rothman
transcript.en: I don't know, I thought you were cooking.
transcript.zh: 我不知道啊，我还以为是你下厨呢。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Oh no, I am not cooking, Andy. Yeah, it's going to be really good Beijing food. It's the place across the street.
transcript.zh: 别闹了，我可不下厨，Andy。不过今晚肯定是顿地道的北京菜。就在马路对面的那家店。

transcript.speaker: Andy Rothman
transcript.en: I'm here for some good Beijing food.
transcript.zh: 我来这儿就是想吃点地道的北京菜。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I count myself really blessed that one of my very favorite restaurants in town, it's really down-home basic Beijing food, but they specialize in something called dalian huoshao. Dalian huoshao are sort of like elongated guotie, and they're delicious. They have every variety of stuffing you can imagine, and they've got good Peking duck. Anyway, we are on our way to dinner, so talk soon.
transcript.zh: 我觉得自己特别有口福，全城我最喜欢的餐馆之一就在附近，那是很家常地道的北京风味，但他们的招牌是褡裢火烧。褡裢火烧有点像长条形的锅贴，味道绝了。你能想到的馅儿他们全都有，烤鸭也做得不错。总之，我们正赶去吃晚饭，回头再聊。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So dinner was just such a lively conversation with really candid exchanges of ideas that I decided maybe not to pull out the mic and ruin it. But I did get reacquainted with someone I'd met on a few occasions, the economist Zhu Ning, who is now at Shanghai Jiao Tong University. A brilliant guy with wide-ranging experience, a really interesting career, who I will have on the show in the future.
transcript.zh: 晚饭时的交流实在太热烈了，大家的思想交锋非常坦诚，所以我觉得还是别掏出麦克风来破坏气氛了。不过，我借机重新结识了一位之前见过几次的朋友——经济学家朱宁。他目前在上海交通大学任教，才华横溢，阅历极广，履历非常精彩，我以后一定会请他上节目聊聊。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: He had one of the most interesting ideas that I've heard in a while. It was connecting the deliberate deflation of the real estate bubble, you know, beginning with the Three Red Lines policy back six years ago, with China's push into AI, into advanced semiconductors, and all the other hard tech that China's been really obsessed with over the last several years. I'll be sure to get him to spell that all out when I get him on the show finally.
transcript.zh: 他提出了一个我很久没听过的、极为引人深思的观点。他将中国主动刺破房地产泡沫的做法——比如六年前出台的‘三道红线’政策——与中国近年来大力进军AI、先进制程半导体以及整个国家在过去几年深度痴迷的各类‘硬科技’联系了起来。等他最终上了节目，我一定会让他把这一逻辑彻底剖析清楚。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So it was an action-packed weekend, it being Halloween, but you're going to have to take my word for it. My recorder's battery died while I was still at the Golden Weasel, having a quiet drink after dinner, and I really should have just switched over to my phone's voice memo app, damn it. Anthony and Dan, the bar's owners, had been told explicitly not to do anything Halloween-themed. There's been in recent years an effort to discourage the celebration of foreign holidays in Beijing at least, and I guess I hear this is true in some other cities as well.
transcript.zh: 那是个精彩纷呈的万圣节周末，但大家只能听我口述了。晚饭后我在金鼬酒吧喝杯酒歇会儿时，录音机没电了——真该死，我当时真应该直接切到手机语音备忘录录音的。酒吧老板Anthony和Dan接到明确通知，不能举办任何万圣节主题活动。近年来，至少在北京，有关方面一直不提倡过‘洋节’，据我所知其他一些城市似乎也是如此。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So the Weasel was relatively quiet for a Saturday night. And at around 11 p.m., a few of us headed over to Time Keepers, which is another favorite spot of mine, right by the old Drum and Bell Towers on Beijing's central axis. It's a great place.
transcript.zh: 因此，作为一个周六的夜晚，金鼬酒吧显得相对安静。到了夜里11点左右，我们几个人转场去了‘拾光客’（Time Keepers），这也是我最喜欢的去处之一，紧挨着北京中轴线上的钟鼓楼，地方很棒。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: The place was just completely hopping though that night. A bunch of Schwarzman Scholars had come down from distant Haidian, and I chatted with several who were doing very cool capstone projects, and were really thrilled about their faculty advisors. One had Dean Shi and was working on something related to AI governance, and another had Susan Shirk, who, of course, listeners will know.
transcript.zh: 不过那晚店里真是热闹非凡。一群来自远在海淀的苏世民学者聚在那儿，我和其中几位聊了聊，他们正在做的毕业课题非常硬核，对自己导师的评价也极高。其中一位的导师是薛澜院长，研究方向是AI治理；另一位的导师则是本节目听众非常熟悉的Susan Shirk。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And they were generally very enthusiastic, understandably, about being at Schwarzman. So, a shout out to Sue and to Gaston, and some of the others who I chatted with that night. Wish I'd had my batteries.
transcript.zh: 他们整体上对能在苏世民书院学习感到非常兴奋，这完全可以理解。所以，向 Sue、Gaston 以及当晚和我聊天的其他人打个招呼。真希望当时录音机有电池。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So, it's Sunday afternoon now. About a week or so ago, I got a note in email from my friend Eric Fish, who actually I knew in Beijing ages ago. He came just before the Olympics, I believe.
transcript.zh: 现在是周日下午了。大约一周前，我收到了朋友 Eric Fish 发来的一封邮件。其实我很久以前就在北京认识他了，他好像是奥运会前夕过来的。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: He and his wife ended up moving to the Research Triangle, to Cary in North Carolina. There was a group of us there: Elise Ribbans, who was an old friend of mine in Beijing, she'd gone to high school actually in Chapel Hill and ended up moving back there, and we overlapped for some time. Eric, a couple of other people, too. So, it was sort of a nice thing to have some old Beijing friends in Chapel Hill.
transcript.zh: 后来他和妻子搬到了北卡罗来纳州三角研究园的卡里。我们当时有一群人在那里：Elise Ribbans，也是我在北京的老朋友，她其实是在教堂山读的高中，后来又搬回了那里，我们有一段时间住得挺近。还有 Eric 以及其他几个人。所以在教堂山能有一群北京老友，感觉真的很棒。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: He was coming to Beijing, so we arranged for him to come to my favorite Sichuan restaurant in town. It's a Chongqing restaurant technically, it's called Sanyang Cai. If you're ever in Beijing, you've got to try Sanyang Cai.
transcript.zh: 他这次来北京，我们就约好去城里我最喜欢的一家川菜馆。严格来说是一家重庆菜馆，叫“三样菜”。如果你来北京，一定要尝尝三样菜。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Anyway, Eric is with me here at lunch. It's Sunday and the wind blew up overnight, it got kind of chilly. But you haven't been back here in eight years, is that right?
transcript.zh: 总之，Eric 正在和我一起吃午饭。今天是周日，昨晚刮起了大风，天气有点凉了。不过你已经有八年没回来了，是吧？

transcript.speaker: Eric Fish
transcript.en: Yeah, that's right. It's been a minute.
transcript.zh: 对，没错。确实很久了。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So, okay. I mean, it's cliché now, but impressions, first impressions? Or, you know, you've only been here for a couple of days, but I'm often very curious about what people, you know... I hadn't been away for four years, and people were constantly asking me for my impressions. I often didn't know what the fuck to say. But here, what do you think? What's going on here?
transcript.zh: 好吧，我知道这问题很老套，但第一印象如何？你才刚来几天，不过我经常很好奇大家的感受……我当年不过是离开了四年，大家就老是问我的感受，我常常都不知道他妈的该怎么回答。但说说看，你怎么看？这里现在感觉怎么样？

transcript.speaker: Eric Fish
transcript.en: I mean, it's some of the obvious stuff people often mention. The technology has definitely changed by leaps and bounds. It's like everything is so seamless. The cars that you see on the street are wild, like all kinds of different shapes and sizes, and grades of electric power, which is kind of interesting.
transcript.zh: 我是说，有些确实是大家经常提及的显而易见的方面。科技层面绝对是突飞猛进。感觉一切衔接都极其丝滑。街上跑的汽车太夸张了，各种形状、尺寸，还有不同纯电技术规格的电动车，挺有意思的。

transcript.speaker: Eric Fish
transcript.en: But at the same time, I'm kind of surprised at what hasn't changed so much. It's like a lot of the constant construction that marked most of the time I lived here has all kind of completed. And the real estate markets really jumped out at me, too, like how dirt cheap a lot of the housing has gotten because of the collapse of the real estate bubble.
transcript.zh: 但与此同时，我也有些惊讶于很多东西其实并没有怎么变。比如我住在这里时大部分时间随处可见的施工，现在基本都完工了。房地产市场也让我印象极其深刻，因为房地产泡沫破裂，很多房子的价格跌得极其厉害。

transcript.speaker: Eric Fish
transcript.en: Like, meeting people with multiple houses they can't unload. So, that's been one thing. I do hear from the young people kind of disillusion, but that's been a perpetual story for 20 years. People are kind of pessimistic about the economy, but like I said, that's been a constant story for a while.
transcript.zh: 比如碰到手里有多套房却脱不了手的人。这是其一。我也确实从年轻人那里听到了一些幻灭感，但这在过去20年里一直都是老生常谈了。大家对经济有点悲观，不过就像我说的，这种论调也存在一阵子了。

transcript.speaker: Eric Fish
transcript.en: Yeah, I don't know. But the general vibe, the conversation that I'm having, I'm kind of surprised what hasn't changed. But that's kind of the cliché with China, like it changes so much in some ways, and then some things just never change.
transcript.zh: 是啊，我说不好。但整体的氛围、我们进行的这些谈话，我倒挺惊讶于那些没变的东西。但这大概也是关于中国的老生常谈了：在某些方面变化翻天覆地，而在另一些方面又似乎永远如旧。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: You wrote a book a while back on China's millennials, basically. In fact, the book was...
transcript.zh: 你前些年写过一本关于中国千禧一代的书，基本上是这个主题。事实上，那本书的书名是……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: China's millennials and you've taken an interest in the next generation, sort of Gen Z in China and you're working on that for a while. That was pre-COVID, and then of course things have changed a lot. Are you still trying to sort of understand kids these days? Is that is that your main thing still?
transcript.zh: 中国的千禧一代，而且你对下一代，也就是中国的Z世代也产生了兴趣，你在这方面做了一阵子研究。那是疫情前的事了，当然从那之后情况发生了很大变化。你现在还在努力去理解如今的年轻一代吗？这依然是你的主要研究方向吗？

transcript.speaker: Eric Fish
transcript.en: Yeah, always. I mean, I think when a society is changing like so, well, at any speed, you see it most acutely in the youth that are being, like coming of age, being shaped by that environment. I just think that's been true in China. That's always been a story, like the generation gaps just 5 years apart between people, so that's always kind of who I look to to see how things are evolving in society.
transcript.zh: 对，一直都是。我觉得当一个社会在发生转变时——无论以何种速度——你总能在正在成长、被环境所塑造的年轻人身上最敏锐地捕捉到这种变化。我觉得在中国尤为如此，这里一直都有这样的现象，哪怕只相差五岁，人与人之间也会有代沟。所以我总是把目光投向他们，以此观察社会的变化轨迹。

transcript.speaker: Eric Fish
transcript.en: But yeah, I mean, now that I'm getting older and like I'm a generation above the young people, I don't know, there's like a lot of constant themes. Like I said, there does seem to be a perpetual sense of disillusionment and, um, but, I don't know.
transcript.zh: 不过话说回来，随着我年纪渐长，比当下的年轻人整整大了一代，我发现这其中有很多恒久不变的主题。就像我之前说的，似乎总有一种挥之不去的幻灭感，但是，我也说不好。

transcript.speaker: Eric Fish
transcript.en: The the crowd I've been looking at the last several years has been like Chinese international students in the US, so that's been like an interesting dynamic on top of that, like how to bridge these two countries and kind of it's more and more felt like kids with divorcing parents being pulled from both directions. Like more and more feel like they have to choose one or the other, harder to live a transnational life. So I don't know, that's the the theme I've been researching.
transcript.zh: 这几年我一直在关注的群体是在美中国留学生，在此背景下这成了一种很有趣的互动——比如如何在这两国之间搭建桥梁。感觉他们越来越像离异家庭的孩子，被两边拉扯；越来越多的人觉得非此即彼，必须二选一，跨国生活变得越发艰难。所以，这就是我一直在研究的主题。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah, the story of my life, right? Trying to knit together the two sides of your of your soul. Eric, man, welcome back. What are some of the things you feel like you need to do before you move out from Beijing?
transcript.zh: 是啊，这简直就是我的人生写照，努力把灵魂撕裂的两半重新缝合在一起。Eric，哥们儿，欢迎回来。离开北京之前，你觉得自己还有哪些必做清单吗？

transcript.speaker: Eric Fish
transcript.en: Oh, God. Well, I mean eating Sichuan food was the the top of the list, so you've taken care of that for me. Um, but I don't know, just checking out the old haunts, what's still there, what's not. That is one kind of a bummer about Beijing is, like, a lot of the the old places you hang out disappear, but in of a dynamic city that's always changing, so.
transcript.zh: 天呐，吃川菜本来是排在第一位的，结果你已经替我安排好了。不过别的嘛，就是去常去的旧地逛逛，看看哪些还在，哪些已经没了。北京确实有这么一点让人挺遗憾的，很多你以前常去扎堆的老地方都消失了，但这也证明它是一座充满活力、不断变化的城市。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And then so many of us were drawn to Beijing because of the rapidity of change to begin with, so we sort of can't have our cake and eat it, too, right? It's going to change around us and and we're going to feel lost, but hey. Thanks, man. It was great to see you.
transcript.zh: 而且，我们当初之所以被北京吸引，本身也是因为这种飞速的变化，所以我们不能两头占便宜，对吧？身边的环境总会变，我们也会感到迷茫失落，但人生就是这样。谢了哥们儿，能见到你真高兴。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: All right. So, that's basically it. I I treat myself most Mondays though to a kind of weekend aftershock. Time Keepers, where I ended up on Saturday night, that's called Sāngōng in Chinese, has a terrific open mic on Monday nights. It's a great mix of of of Chinese and foreign talent who all converge in that place, you know, to jam or to belt out a tune.
transcript.zh: 好的，本期内容大概就是这些了。不过大多数周一，我都会给自己来一场周末的“余震”。周六晚上我最后去的 Time Keepers——中文叫“三更”——在周一晚上有一场特别棒的开放麦。那里汇聚了来自中外各路的才艺高手，大家聚在一起即兴合奏或是引吭高歌。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Of late, I have had the pleasure of playing along with Sasso in the kind of informal house band. The host of the event, this guy, he's a Ugandan guy with an amazing voice and a huge repertoire of songs that basically has zero overlap
transcript.zh: 最近我有幸跟 Sasso 一起在非正式的驻场乐队里伴奏。这个活动的组织者是个乌干达小伙，嗓音绝了，掌握的曲目量大得惊人，基本上跟我的曲库完全没有任何重合。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: With my repertoire, but they're great tunes. Mostly kind of reggae-ish stuff, some soul, even some stuff I suppose would be classed as gospel. But you know, I could figure out the chords and he gives me a solo here and there.
transcript.zh: 虽然不在我的拿手曲目里，但都是很棒的歌。大多带点雷鬼风，有些灵魂乐，甚至还有些我觉得能归为福音音乐的东西。不过我能摸出和弦，他也时不时让我弹一段独奏。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And I've heard just amazing singers come through. There's this Irish guy named Dave who I think is a teacher here. Dave came up a couple weeks ago, and he did this gorgeous rendition of America by Simon and Garfunkel that really brought tears to my eyes.
transcript.zh: 我还听到了很多极其出色的歌手登台。有位叫 Dave 的爱尔兰小哥，我猜他在这边当老师。Dave 几周前上台，翻唱了 Simon and Garfunkel 的《America》，唱得太动人了，简直让我热泪盈眶。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I mean, that's like my favorite song, just flat-out my favorite song. If you are in Beijing, come check out that open mic. I guess I should throw in a recommendation, yeah?
transcript.zh: 那真的是我最喜欢的歌，不折不扣的最爱。如果你在北京，一定要来这个开放麦瞧瞧。我想我是不是该给个推荐了，对吧？

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I am now reading The Master and Margarita by Mikhail Bulgakov at the recommendation of the wonderful Marina Rudyak, with whom I had dinner last week. You might remember Marina from one of the early Ukraine post-full-scale invasion shows.
transcript.zh: 我最近在读 Mikhail Bulgakov 的《大师与玛格丽特》，这是优秀的 Marina Rudyak 推荐给我的，我上周刚和她吃了晚饭。大家可能还记得 Marina，她曾在乌克兰全面战争爆发后早期的几期节目中做客。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: She was in town along with her colleague Nadine and a former Sinica intern named Ollie Dieckmann. Make that my paying it forward: Ollie is terrific, he's a really promising young researcher.
transcript.zh: 她这次和同事 Nadine 以及 Sinica 前实习生 Ollie Dieckmann 一起来了北京。这也算是我的一种传承与提携吧：Ollie 非常棒，是一位前途无量的年轻研究员。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: This is a terrifically funny novel, just to get back to The Master and Margarita. It lurches between, you know, really big philosophical ideas and then basically slapstick humor.
transcript.zh: 回到《大师与玛格丽特》，这是一部极其幽默的小说。它在宏大的哲学命题与近乎闹剧般的荒谬幽默之间来回穿梭。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So Marina, who was born in Russia, says it's her favorite Russian novel, and I can definitely see why. It is quite a contrast from the last enormous doorstop of a novel that I read from Russia, which was called Stalingrad by Vasily Grossman.
transcript.zh: Marina 出生于俄罗斯，她说这是她最喜欢的俄罗斯小说，我完全理解。这和我之前读过的那本像门挡一样厚重的俄罗斯大部头——Vasily Grossman 的《斯大林格勒》——形成了鲜明对比。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I am off to Mexico City for a conference about podcasts of all things, which sounds like it's going to be a lot of fun. So probably no show next week, but I do have something great for the following week. I'm speaking again with Joe Studwell, I mentioned that. There are more shows in the pipeline, so thank you for spending the weekend with me, and I'll see you soon.
transcript.zh: 我马上要去墨西哥城参加一个专门关于播客的研讨会，听起来会非常有意思。所以下周可能没有常规节目，但我为下下周准备了重磅内容。我会再次与 Joe Studwell 对话，之前提过这事。还有更多节目正在制作中，感谢大家陪我度过这个周末，我们很快再见！

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: You've been listening to the Sinica Podcast. The show is produced, recorded, engineered, edited, and mastered by me, Kaiser Kuo. Support the show through Substack at sinicapodcast.com, where there is a growing offering of terrific original China-related writing and audio.
transcript.zh: 您收听的是 Sinica Podcast。本节目由我 Kaiser Kuo 制作、录音、工程混音、剪辑和母带处理。欢迎通过 Substack（网址：sinicapodcast.com）支持我们，那里有越来越多精彩的原创涉华文章和音频内容。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Or email me at sinicapod@gmail.com if you've got ideas on how you can help out with the show, or if you're in Beijing and you want to meet up. Don't forget to leave a review on Apple Podcasts.
transcript.zh: 如果您对如何协助制作节目有任何想法，或者您正好在北京想要见个面，欢迎发邮件至 sinicapod@gmail.com。别忘了在 Apple Podcasts 上留下好评。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Huge thanks to all the people who allowed me to stick a mic in their face and chat with them. Thanks for listening, and we'll see you next week. Take care.
transcript.zh: 非常感谢所有愿意让我把麦克风递到面前并与我畅谈的朋友们。感谢您的收听，我们下周见。保重！

vocab_notes.meaning_zh: 令人不快；激怒；引人反感
vocab_notes.note_zh: 源自动物颈部毛发立起的生理反应，常用于指某种观点、言论或行为触碰敏感神经、引发受众的抵触与反感。
清洁能源与建筑工程术语，指将太阳能光伏发电产品直接集成或整合为建筑物外立面、屋顶等建材的一部分。

vocab_notes.meaning_zh: 风土条件；特定产区微气候与土壤特征
vocab_notes.note_zh: 源自法语，原本专门用于葡萄酒品鉴，形容土壤、气候、日照等自然环境对作物品质风味的影响，后被延伸至精酿威士忌等烈酒领域。
社会学概念，指家庭（第一空间）和工作场所（第二空间）之外，供人们社交聚会、放松交流的公共或半公共场所（如酒吧、咖啡馆）。
国际政治经济学前沿概念，指大国利用全球化网络中的不对称枢纽节点（如金融支付体系、关键技术供应链），将其转变为施加地缘政治强制力的工具。
宏观经济学术语，用来描述经济衰退或复苏过程中不同阶层、行业或群体走向极度分化（一部分快速上升、一部分持续下挫）。
中国央行和住建部于2020年出台的房企融资监管政策指标（剔除预收款后的资产负债率、净负债率、现金短债比），旨在防范房地产金融化泡沫风险。

vocab_notes.meaning_zh: 大部头厚重书籍（俚语，字面意为‘门挡’）
vocab_notes.note_zh: 英语出版与文学圈常用俗语，幽默地形容那些厚重、篇幅极其庞大的书，甚至重得可以拿来顶门挡风。
